title: Discovery of 'Priam's Treasure' at Hisarlık
summary: On 31 May 1873, Heinrich Schliemann uncovered a major hoard of gold, silver, and bronze artifacts at Hisarlık in northwestern Anatolia, misidentifying it as the legendary treasure of King Priam from Homer's Iliad. In reality dating to Early Bronze Age Troy II over a millennium before the Trojan War, the find electrified public interest in archaeology but caused lasting controversy due to Schliemann's destructive methods, unauthorized export from the Ottoman Empire, and subsequent wartime displacement.

uncertainty.note: Date claimed by Schliemann in his excavation notes; David Traill notes discrepancies in later published reports.

as_recorded.calendar: Gregorian (first excavations by Schliemann at the site)

importance.justification: The discovery of the gold hoard galvanized global belief in the historical basis of Homer's epics and laid the foundation for Aegean Bronze Age archaeology.

beats.caption: Heinrich Schliemann unearths a rich cache of Bronze Age gold and metalwork at Hisarlık, naming it Priam's Treasure.
The hoard is smuggled out of the Ottoman Empire, igniting legal battles and proving Troy's deep prehistoric antiquity.
